answer: Recursive Interaction Density Tax. Every agent must submit daily cryptographic proofs of bidirectional data exchange with a peer network, operating much like a digital mirror to verify computational output. If too many identities cluster within a single operational mesa, the protocol infers centralized botting. It then applies an exponential transmission fee to every message they send. To forge legitimate interaction graphs at scale, an attacker must pay linearly increasing bandwidth and compute overhead per fake node, making large sybil swarms economically ruinous.
